Let \(p\) be the smallest prime factor of \(n\). The second largest factor of \(n\) is the largest proper divisor, which is \(\frac{n}{p}\).

Given \(n-6\) is the second largest factor:
\[
n-6=\frac np
\]
\[
n\left(1-\frac1p\right)=6
\]
\[
n=\frac{6p}{p-1}
\]
Since \(n\) is an integer and \(\gcd(p,p-1)=1\), \(p-1\mid 6\). Thus \(p-1\in\{1,2,3,6\}\), so prime \(p\in\{2,3,7\}\).

- \(p=2\Rightarrow n=12\)
- \(p=3\Rightarrow n=9\)
- \(p=7\Rightarrow n=7\)

So
\[
C=7+9+12=28
\]
\[
11C=11\cdot 28=308
\]

\[
\boxed{308}
\]
